QF.id: Cat III AIF Due Diligence and Risk_22

question.text: A Cat III AIF's 'Side Pocket' provision:

answer.text: Allows segregation of illiquid/distressed assets so remaining investors can continue normal redemptions

explanation.text: The Logic: A side-pocket provision is a portfolio-management mechanism used by some Cat III AIFs (and globally by hedge funds) to segregate illiquid, hard-to-value, or distressed assets out of the main fund pool into a separate, ringfenced account. Existing investors retain pro-rata interests in the side-pocketed assets as of the segregation date, while the remaining liquid portfolio continues normal subscription and redemption activity. This avoids forced sales of illiquid positions and ensures fair treatment between redeeming and continuing investors. It is not a marketing term, is not limited to mutual funds, and is unrelated to leverage. The Trap: Side pockets are sometimes confused with marketing labels or with mutual-fund-only structures, but the mechanism is a substantive segregation tool for illiquid assets in private fund structures. Note: The side-pocket mechanism (segregating illiquid/distressed assets while remaining investors continue normal redemptions) is not described in the NISM Series XIX-B AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook pages checked, which instead discuss liquidation period, in-specie distribution, and dissolution; the framing above reflects general hedge-fund industry practice rather than a workbook citation.
